newsitem.title: CHINA: China says it unlikely to halt import slide in 97.
newsitem.headline: China says it unlikely to halt import slide in 97.

text.p: China was unlikely to halt a decline in imports this year, though exports will continue to make gains, a trade official said on Wednesday quoting a white paper on China's foreign economic and trade.

The white paper, currently being prepared by the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, concludes that the drop in imports partly reflects strong competition from domestic manufacturers which have managed to improve their product quality while maintaining competitive prices.
This is particularly evident in the machinery and electronic industry, the official told Reuters.
Imports in the first four months of this year dipped 0.5 percent from a year ago to $40 billion. Exports during the same period climbed by 26.9 percent to $50.26 billion, official trade data show.
The ministry official also said that imports are likely to climb sharply once China joins the World Trade Organisation (WTO). China is still negotiating terms for its long-sought goal of joining WTO.
China's target for total trade this year is $310 billion compared with $289.9 billion last year, according to the white paper.
The document also puts actual utilisation of foreign investment this year at $30 billion, the official said.
